name: Marduk
title: Babylon's chief god
summary: Marduk (also called Merodach) was the supreme deity in the Babylonian pantheon and the patron god of Babylon. In the Bible, he is mentioned as an idol that God judges in connection with the fall of Babylon. His name appears in compound personal names such as Merodach-Baladan and Evil-Merodach.

keyEvents.title: God's judgment against Marduk (Merodach)
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah proclaimed the fall of Babylon and declared that Marduk (Merodach) would be broken and humiliated.

keyEvents.title: Bel bows down
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesied that Bel (another name for Marduk) would bow down and his idol would be humiliated when Babylon fell.

keyEvents.title: Merodach-Baladan sends envoys to Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: Merodach-Baladan, a Babylonian king named after the god Marduk, sent letters and gifts to King Hezekiah of Judah after his illness.

keyEvents.title: Evil-Merodach Releases Jehoiachin
keyEvents.description: Evil-Merodach (Amel-Marduk), a Babylonian king named after the god Marduk, released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison and showed him kindness.

keyEvents.title: Daniel in Babylon Among Idolaters
keyEvents.description: Daniel and his friends were taken to Babylon, where Marduk was the chief god, but they remained faithful to the God of Israel and refused to worship idols.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Mockery of Babylon's Idols
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah mocked the idols in Babylon, including Marduk/Bel, and declared that they were powerless compared to the living God of Israel who carries His people.
